title: Fed vortices with a continuous trait: a whole-vortex, trait-blind mutation makes vortices pure (within-vortex trait spread ~0.01) and daughters keep the parent's trait class at 96-97% of splits; under a saturating gain advantage the dominant class steps 0->1->2->3->4(5) over T=6000 on 2/2 seeds while the identical-draw twin stays at class 0; an unbounded (linear) advantage climbs into the coarsening regime and destroys the individuals
summary: world.py is c53's fed-vortex selection world with the two labels replaced by a label density c and a trait mass z (theta = z/c), copied only where the vortex eats by a term linear in z (so the copy carries theta and never reads it), and a trait-blind mutation every 50 t that shifts theta by +-0.4 over the whole vortex under a randomly drawn eating pixel. Gain is k(1 + eps tanh theta). trait.py (labkit segmentation and tracker, as c53's heredity.py) on seeds 1-2, T=6000: favoured eps 0.3 vs the identical-draw eps 0 twin: mean vortex trait after t=4000 1.29/1.33 vs 0.14/0.00, dominant class (theta/0.4) reaches 4-5 vs stays 0; daughters within 0.2 of the parent's trait 115/118 and 96/101 (twin 120/151, 155/202), parent-daughter r 0.98/0.98 (twin 0.85/0.87), within-vortex trait spread median 0.016/0.018 (twin 0.002/0.003); all trait jumps of living vortices are +-0.40 (mutations). With a linear gain k(1 + 0.2 theta) the trait climbs faster but once mean theta passes ~1.5 the vortices coarsen into a few domain-filling blobs (labelled vortices 30 -> 1-8; seed 2 a single blob from t~3400), so selection on gain is self-limiting here.

finding.operator: continuous trait carried as a label density c and trait mass z copied linearly where the vortex eats; whole-vortex trait-blind mutation (+-0.4)
finding.control: identical-draw neutral twin (eps 0, same mutation draws), seeds 1 2; linear-fitness arm
finding.result: favoured eps 0.3: mean trait t>=4000 1.29/1.33, dominant class 0->4/5 in steps (trait_maps_s1.png); twin 0.14/0.00, class 0; daughter class fidelity 97%/95% (twin 79%/77%); within-vortex spread 0.016/0.018; linear eps 0.2 collapses to 1-8 vortices after mean trait ~1.5

limits: Two seeds, 128^2, one parameter point; no dt/2 or grid test. The fitness effect is written (the trait scales the gain) and saturates (tanh), so the climb has a ceiling: seed 1 plateaus at theta ~1.3-1.5 after t=3300 and the dominant class then alternates between 3 and 4. This is a finite series of sweeps, not open-endedness, and the linear form shows that an unbounded gain advantage ends the individuals rather than continuing. Where selection acts is not yet measured: the parents of persistent splits are not above the population mean trait (0.51, 0.42 favoured vs 0.41, 0.56 twin), so the rise may run through fusions (the larger, higher-gain vortex dominates the fused trait), area growth or survival rather than birth rate; trait.py did not record per-frame traits in these runs, so per-capita births per class are not computed. Higher-theta vortices are rods and the favoured world is more crowded (pack_sel occupancy 0.40). The twin's lower daughter fidelity (77-79%) is unexplained; it may come from labkit counting re-separations of fused vortices of different traits as splits. The 'jumps elsewhere' counts in the eps 0.3 json files (24, 25) come from the first version of the mutation matcher (15 px from the drawn pixel); every one is a step of +-0.40 (jumps_elsewhere_sizes), i.e. a whole-vortex mutation on a large vortex; the corrected matcher (by time) gives 0 in the linear runs.
